extraction_notes: Family datasheet covers S3AB through S3MB; the S3MB column applies: VRRM = 1000 V, VRMS = 700 V, VDC = 1000 V. All electrical-characteristics rows (VF, IR, CJ) are shared across the family.

Absolute maximum ratings (p. 1, Ta = 25 degC): IF(AV) = 3.0 A (60 Hz half sine, resistive load, TL per Fig.1), IFSM = 100 A (8.3 ms single half sine), Tj and Tstg = -55 to +150 degC, RthJA = 60 degC/W, RthJL = 25 degC/W (5.0 x 5.0 mm pads).

Curves digitized programmatically from a 300 dpi render of page 2. Axes calibrated from the gridline family; decade gridlines landed within 1% of their nominal values (10/1.0/0.1 checks). Curve stroke (4 px) separated from gridlines (2 px) by run length, tracked column-to-column to reject legend text.

Fig.3 digitized typical curve is consistent with the table limit: digitized VF at 3.0 A is about 1.00 V versus the 1.0 V maximum table value, so the plotted 'typical' curve effectively traces the maximum limit; treat it as generic family artwork with that caveat.

Fig.4 x-axis is percent of rated peak reverse voltage; for S3MB, 100% = 1000 V. Both curves were digitized up to 122%; above roughly 128-130% of rated voltage both curves turn into a near-vertical breakdown wall, which was not digitized, and no numeric breakdown voltage or current is specified in the datasheet, so breakdown_voltage and breakdown_current are null.
The 125 degC reverse curve and the 200 uA @ 125 degC table row are recorded for reference; per archetype-diode.md the high-temperature IR row must not be used for fitting.
No reverse recovery time is specified anywhere in the datasheet (standard-recovery general purpose rectifier), so reverse_recovery is null.
